producer_report.summary: Fixed at the reading gate: a new check, `check_scope_limit`, refuses a change reading whose file-scope limit leaves out files the job must change anyway. Root cause: a scope limit was written from the named files without listing default-written files and config consumers, and nothing at the gate compared it with CHANGELOG.md (which Athena always writes) or with the readers of a changed config. The check refuses a limit that lists its allowed files without CHANGELOG.md or 'the deliverables'. It also refuses an athena.toml or defaults.toml deliverable under a limit with no valid `Consumers:` assumption. It is one `step!` in `refusing_check`, reads the limit through a new single matcher `change_limit` in briefs.rs (which `limits_changed_files` now wraps), and has a new reader rule line, unit tests, 25 corpus cases, a CHANGELOG entry and decision D166. The scope tests' LIMIT constant in run/tests.rs now names CHANGELOG.md because it goes through the real gate. fmt, clippy, the full suite and the policy scan pass. The refusal share is not measured here; the verification replay measures it.

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs defines `check_scope_limit` with a doc comment that names the root cause (a scope limit written from the named files without listing default-written files and config consumers) and cites jobs 20261018-045437-7z81 and 20261023-052543-9bw7, and `refusing_check` calls it as a single `step!(check_scope_limit(..))` line.
criteria_check.evidence: Read checks.rs: pub fn check_scope_limit has the doc block with the root-cause sentence and both job ids; refusing_check has `step!(check_scope_limit(reading));`. Run `cargo test -p athena-core scope_limit_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause scope_limit_has_one_step_line`: both pass (the doc test reads the doc block from checks.rs by include_str!, the other counts the single step line).

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs builds a reading with a scope-limit criterion and no CHANGELOG.md deliverable and asserts refusing_check returns "check_scope_limit"; the same reading with CHANGELOG.md listed is accepted. The test fails when the step! line is removed.
criteria_check.evidence: scope_limit_changelog in reading.rs asserts gate_refuser == Some("check_scope_limit") for a limit reading with no CHANGELOG.md deliverable and for production-shaped ones, and None once the limit names CHANGELOG.md or 'the deliverables'. 'Listed' is read as named in the limit's allowed words, because ensure_changelog always lists the deliverable before the gate (explained in the changelog and D166). I commented out the step line and ran `cargo test -p athena-core scope_limit`: scope_limit_changelog failed (left None, right Some("check_scope_limit")); I then restored the line.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test builds a reading with a modify deliverable athena.toml, a scope limit, and neither a crates/ test deliverable nor a `Consumers:` assumption, and asserts it is refused by check_scope_limit; adding either makes it pass. A reading without a scope limit and a reading with no config deliverable are unaffected.

Revised sense: a bare test deliverable alone stays refused, a Consumers line is the answer (departure recorded in D166 and the changelog). Passed in `cargo test -p athena-core --lib scope_limit`; failed with the step removed.

criteria_check.criterion: git diff shows no change to athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, records/, or the files kept from job 20261018-045437-7z81 beyond what is listed as deliverables.
criteria_check.evidence: git diff --stat lists seven files: CHANGELOG.md, briefs.rs, reading.rs, checks.rs, run/tests.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, docs/decisions.md. No athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, records/, proposals.rs, steward.rs or 7z81 file appears. run/tests.rs is the one file outside the six listed deliverables (a forced one-constant edit, reported in open_issues).

open_issues: The share of past readings newly refused is not measured by the producer: the snapshot has no records/ or history. The verification replay measures it (hold above 8%, declared 3% is an estimate). I did not narrow the check or edit the declared figure.

crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs is outside the six deliverables of the accepted reading; its LIMIT constant had to name CHANGELOG.md because the scope tests go through the real gate. If the scope guard treats the deliverable list as an allowlist, add it to the reading.

Departures from the accepted reading, recorded in D166 and the changelog: out_of_scope items are not scanned (verification reads criteria only); 'CHANGELOG.md listed' is read as named in the limit's allowed words (ensure_changelog always lists the deliverable); a bare test deliverable alone does not satisfy the config half, a Consumers line is needed; defaults-proposal jobs now need one Consumers line (for example 'Consumers: none found').

Known misses, recorded in D166: a bare form that really forbids CHANGELOG.md, a negation inside the allowed words, a second limiting criterion, and no verification that a 'none found' line followed a search.
A proposed job whose latest stored reading has such a limit leaves the drain queue until it is read again (queued_work re-checks stored readings).
mistakes: A closure in the first draft of scope_limit_config_consumers did not compile (lifetime of a borrowed slice); I fixed it with 'static types before any test ran.
I first wrote the doc comment's share sentence with a capital 'Expected', which would not match the 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' needle; I reworded it before running the doc test.
learnings: ensure_changelog (reading.rs) adds a CHANGELOG.md deliverable before the gate, so a check on the deliverable list alone can never refuse; the gate has to read the limit text.
The verification-time allowed list is the deliverable list, built from the first limiting criterion only (limiting_criterion / allowed_paths in briefs.rs); out_of_scope items are never read.
The run/tests.rs scope tests push LIMIT through the real reading gate through a fake reader, so any new reading rule that refuses a limit phrase needs that constant updated.
READING_RULES is written only into the reader brief, so adding a line costs no reader-prompt tokens; its test bounds each line at 220 bytes and the section size.

Bash here denies heredocs, pipes and tail, and the background task output file is outside the working directory and cannot be read; a foreground cargo command can return 'no build slot free' while another job builds and has to be retried.
desires: A way to run the replay of stored accepted readings from the producer copy, to measure the newly refused share instead of estimating it.
A way to wait on a background cargo run (the task output file is outside the working directory).
